content.title: 130th Boston Marathon: Three champs defend titles, Korir shatters course record
content.text: It was a Kenyan sweep for the men's and women's divisions in Monday's 130th Boston Marathon as Sharon Lokedi and John Korir defended their titles, with Korir shattering the course record. In the wheelchair divisions, Marcel Hug claimed his ninth victory and Eden Rainbow-Cooper secured her second win.Korir set a new course record with an unofficial time of 2:01:52, besting the previous mark of 2:03:02 from 2011. Alphonce Felix Simbu of Tanzania, 55 seconds back, and 2021 champion Benson Kipruto, another 3 seconds behind him, also were fast enough to better the previous Boston record.The course record is worth an additional $50,000 in prize money. Lokedi took her second straight win with an unofficial time of 2:18:51. Loice Chemnung was second, 44 seconds back, followed by Mary Ngugi-Cooper in third. Zouhair Talbi and Jess McClain ran the fastest times ever for Americans in the men's and women's races, respectively.There were familiar faces crowned champions in the wheelchair divisions, too. Hug's win, with an unofficial time of 1:16:06, puts him just one victory away from tying overall all-time Boston Marathon winner South African wheelchair racer Ernst Van Dyk. American Daniel Romanchuk finished second. Rainbow-Cooper's win with an unofficial time of 1:30:51 follows up on her 2024 victory. Swiss racer Catherine Debrunner finished second. In addition to the world-class professional competitors, about 30,000 other athletes -- hailing from 132 countries and all 50 states, including 4,689 Massachusetts residents -- were aiming to conquer the historic course. What's a win worth?Up to $1,484,500 in prize money will be awarded across various divisions in the 130th Boston Marathon. First-place men and women in the open division will earn $150,000, and winners in the wheelchair division receive $50,000. Korir cashes in on an additional $50,000 bonus because he set a course record. Race updates: ArchivedOther runners, honorees on courseCelebrities who took to the historic course include Chelsea Clinton, who finished in 3:40:52; retired Boston Bruins star Zdeno Chara, who finished with a time of 3:18:00; retired NASA astronaut Suni Williams who finished in 5:52:49; Dropkick Murphys' multi-instrumentalist Jeff DaRosa who finished in 03:40:32; former Team USA soccer player Kristine Lilly who finished in 5:16:32; Boston-based comedian Laura Green who finished in 3:50:17; and "Love Island USA" Season 7 winner Bryan Arenales who finished in 4:06:49, among others. WCVB's A.J. Burnett was also running in his first Boston Marathon on Monday. Charity running is a big dealNearly 200 organizations partner with the Boston Marathon to raise tens of millions of dollars every year. This year, the charity runners account for approximately 10% of the total field size.In 2025, the Bank of America Boston Marathon Official Charity Program reached a new record fundraising level of $50.4 million. Since the Official Charity Program’s inception in 1989, more than $600 million has been raised surrounding the Boston Marathon.Get to know the courseThe legendary Boston Marathon course brings world-class athletes racing through eight Massachusetts cities and towns every year on Patriots' Day.According to the Boston Athletic Association, the point-to-point route through Hopkinton, Ashland, Framingham, Natick, Wellesley, Newton, Brookline and Boston is certified by World Athletics and USA Track and Field.
